title: Enforce frontend/backend layer boundaries with import graph and shrinking route-debt allowlists

acceptanceCriteria.description: One executable TypeScript-AST owner defines and enforces dependency direction from frontend/public contracts through routes, services/policies/read models, adapters/connectors, and persistence, and runs first in the mandatory CI source-of-truth pack.

New frontend imports into backend-private modules fail, while every current exception names its exact source/target, removal PS owner, reason, and a stale-on-removal ratchet; the older card baseline has already shrunk to 17 imports across 12 files.
New route-local database writes fail, and the current 80 writes across 11 route files are pinned by exact route endpoint/site counts, reasons, PS owners, and shrinking count ratchets.

AST/semantic negative controls catch renamed frontend authority for rates/money, selected-rate proof, label/provider choice, inventory, billing finalization, auth/scope/status locks, and provider/store capability routing, while positive display/DTO, provider-adapter, and thin-route fixtures remain allowed.

The two stale PS-279 assertions now inspect actual delegation semantics in createLabelV2Impl and processQueueSendOrder instead of obsolete call syntax, and the PS-279/305/313/320/321/329/335 regression guards pass.

The complete 57-command source-of-truth pack, strict backend/frontend TypeScript, production web build, diff check, and protected-surface audit pass at the exact reviewed implementation SHA with no runtime, migration, provider, customer-data, or shipped/cancelled change.
